## Short on space? Explore the best household storage solutions for small homes, from smart in-home ideas to off-site storage that keeps your things safe.


The[best household storage solutions](https://stownest.com/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=household+storage+solution+) for a small home function in two layers. The first layer consists of making the most of the space you have. This includes using vertical space, using storage space under the bed, and using furniture pieces that have multiple functions. The second layer consists of storing belongings that you don't use all the time in a storage unit that is off site. This includes seasonal belongings, festival decorations, and sentimental belongings. With these two layers, you can keep your small home open and not feel the need to get rid of belongings you don't want to part with.


## **The Small Home Problem Nobody Warns You About**


Nobody bothers to tell you that when you start living in a small flat, you'll tell yourself that it'll be okay. A 1BHK is cosy, a 2BHK is efficient. A compact 2BHK is cool, you'll just have to keep things simple.


As months pass by, things change. One cupboard fills up. Then the space under the bed. Next, the top of the wardrobe. After that, the balcony. Then every inch of floor behind every door. Nothing you've bought is unreasonable. It's just that small homes don't have space to keep the regular things a family collects.


If this is something you relate to, it is not your fault. Your home is small, your things need a place to stay. This guide will help you deal with this, and shows things you can do to alleviate the problem inside your home, and the things you can do if your home finally runs out of room.


## **What You Actually Own**


Take a tour of your house before you start buying any boxes or shelves. When you go through your stuff, you'll see you use or touch some things every day. Others you use maybe once or twice a year. Then there are things you hardly ever touch, but can't bring yourself to throw out. The things you use often or daily deserve the best and most convenient storage. Things you use once or twice a year, don't deserve to be on the first line of storage.


The things you rarely use but can't bring yourself to throw out need special storage. They can be stored out of sight. Where you store things depends on how often you use them. Daily use things should be in convenient storage, and things you use once or twice a year need storage that isn't in the first or second line.


## **Storage Solutions for Small Spaces**


These are ideas that pretty much anyone can implement in their flat, and cost practically nothing to execute.


**Think Horizontally and Go Up**


One of the advantages of living in a small home is you are less encouraged to throw things on the wall. In a small home, stacking and placing things vertically can help save floor space. Any flat surface can be used for shelves or hooks.


**Make Your Bed Work Harder**


The area under your bed is the largest empty space in your bedroom. There are lots of beds now with storage drawers or a base that lifts up. If not, you can use a couple of boxes or bags to store things under the bed.


**Choose Furniture Carefully**


Many Indian homes do this already. A bench or a coffee table that has storage or lifts up, serves two purposes. Every piece of furniture in a small flat should do two things.


**Use the Top of the Wardrobe and the Loft Carefully**


Space is often limited in smaller homes, and it can be easy to become disorganized. The space at the top of cupboards and in lofts can be useful for storing items you don't use often, but this space can easily become cluttered. Use this space judiciously and store items only in labeled boxes, not loose. Keep heavier items lower down. Lofts can also become very damp, especially in the monsoon, which is not good for paper, fabric or wood, so these areas should not be used for storage.


**Rethink the Kitchen**


Small kitchens can be easily disorganized. Use wall hooks for utensils. Utilize the space in your cupboard doors with a rack or tray. Appliances that you use infrequently can also be stored in the kitchen to keep counters clear.


## **When In-Home Storage Stops Being Enough**


There are limits to how organized you can be and still have space issues. At a certain point, it doesn't really matter how clever your storage solutions are. It matters that you're hanging onto too much stuff.


You’ll probably be able to identify when you’ve crossed that line. Your wardrobe won’t close. Your balcony is storage for a gazillion boxes. A guest room is half a storeroom. You’re walking around furniture. You can’t use it, but you’re not ready to get rid of it. You’ve become adept at the art of moving clutter from one part of the room to another.


That’s when you need to get really serious about permanently removing clutter from your home.

## **What's Worth Moving Out**


The best candidates are things that take up a lot of space and don’t earn it. Extra mattresses and beds, rarely used bulky furniture, seasonal items, boxes of books and clothes, and festival decorations. Not to mention family heirlooms that you’re just not ready to decide about. If you’re not sure whether something can be stored, just ask customer support before you book.


## **A Simple Way to Choose Between the Two**


You come across a lot of items during your decluttering process and might ask yourself "Will I need this in the next 3 months?" If the answer is no, then chances are you don't need it and it can go. You are allowed to store it if you aren't sure. You can always make the final decision later. You will start to catch on to what you actually miss. You can read about this method and how to declutter your home to have a more minimalist lifestyle.


## **A Few Tips on Safe Storage**


Before you put items away, clean them if necessary and make sure the fabric is dry. Store fragile items in a way that they won't get broken. Make sure the boxes you use to store items aren't flimsy and labeled. Remove items from drawers and cupboards. Take pictures of items you don't want to part with.


## **Mistakes People Make When Living in a Small Home**


The most common mistake is buying more storage furniture without removing anything first. It just adds more to a room that's already full. Other mistakes include keeping everything “just in case,” using damp lofts for paper and fabric, and leaving seasonal items out all year because there’s nowhere else for them to go.


## **Who Benefits Most**


This two-layer approach most benefits people in 1BHKs and compact 2BHKs, couples and families who’ve outgrown their storage, renters who can’t add built-in cupboards, and people who want a clearer home without losing cherished items.


## **The Best Solution Is Usually a Mix**


There isn’t one perfect answer for a small home. The best household storage solutions for a small home combine the smartest use of the space you’ve got with a safe place for things you don’t need every day. Do that, and a small home can feel calm, and easy to live in.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


**1. What are the best household storage solutions for small homes?**


Effective solutions include the use of vertical storage solutions and multifunctional furniture, as well as the use of off-site storage for items that are used infrequently.


**2. What other storage solutions are available for small flats?**


Look to the walls, floor and ceiling of your flat for storage space, as well as using multifunctional and furniture with built-in storage. Consider using off-site household storage for infrequently used items, freeing up cupboard space.


**3. What should I use off-site household storage for?**


Off-site household storage should be used when your household items have been fully organized and you still do not have enough space due to the presence of bulky items such as seasonal items and sentimental items you do not wish to get rid of.
